extracted.intended_audience: state environmental regulators, power plant owners/operators, compliance professionals, and EPA rule commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and regulatory eligibility/measurement criteria for electric generating units and related terms in an EPA Federal Register rulemaking for the power sector (new, modified, reconstructed, and existing sources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum electrical generating output
rubrics_metrics.description: the maximum electrical generating output that a generator, prime mover, or other electric power production equipment under specific conditions designated by the manufacturer is capable of producing (in MWe, rounded to the nearest tenth) on a steady-state basis and during continuous operation (when not restricted by seasonal or other deratings) as of such installation as specified by the manufacturer of the equipment, or starting from the completion of any subsequent physical change resulting in an increase in the maximum electrical generating output that the equipment is capable of producing on a steady-state basis and during continuous operation (when not restricted by seasonal or other deratings), such increased maximum amount (in MWe, rounded to the nearest tenth) as of such completion as specified by the person conducting the physical change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies units (MWe), rounding (nearest tenth), steady-state and continuous-operation basis, excludes seasonal/other deratings, and covers post-physical-change increased capacity as specified by manufacturer or person conducting the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas
rubrics_metrics.description: means a fluid mixture of hydrocarbons (e.g., methane, ethane, or propane), composed of at least 70 percent methane by volume or that has a gross calorific value between 35 and 41 megajoules (MJ) per dry standard cubic meter (950 and 1,100 Btu per dry standard cubic foot), that maintains a gaseous state under ISO conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also explicitly excludes landfill gas, digester gas, refinery gas, sour gas, blast furnace gas, coal-derived gas, producer gas, coke oven gas, or any gaseous fuel produced in a process which might result in highly variable CO2 content or heating value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas-fired steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: means an electric utility steam generating unit meeting the definition of 'fossil fuel-fired,' that is not a coal-fired or oil-fired steam generating unit, that no longer retains the capability to fire coal after December 31, 2029, and that burns natural gas for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during any continuous 3-calendar-year period after December 31, 2029, or for more than 15.0 percent of the annual heat input during any calendar year after December 31, 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines category membership by fuel use thresholds and post-2029 coal-firing capability; thresholds are percentage-based over specified averaging periods (3-calendar-year average >10% or single-year >15%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Net electric output
rubrics_metrics.description: means the amount of gross generation the generator(s) produce (including, but not limited to, output from steam turbine(s), combustion turbine(s), and gas expander(s)), as measured at the generator terminals, less the electricity used to operate the plant (i.e., auxiliary loads); such uses include fuel handling equipment, pumps, fans, pollution control equipment, other electricity needs, and transformer losses as measured at the transmission side of the step up transformer (e.g., the point of sale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies measurement point (generator terminals) and subtraction of auxiliary loads; lists example auxiliary uses and clarifies measurement at transmission side of step-up transformer (point of sale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Net energy output
rubrics_metrics.description: means: (1) The net electric or mechanical output from the affected facility, plus 100 percent of the useful thermal output measured relative to standard ambient temperature and pressure conditions that is not used to generate additional electric or mechanical output or to enhance the performance of the unit (e.g., steam delivered to an industrial process for a heating application). (2) For combined heat and power facilities where at least 20.0 percent of the total gross or net energy output consists of electric or direct mechanical output and at least 20.0 percent of the total gross or net energy output consists of useful thermal output on a 12-operating month rolling average basis, the net electric or mechanical output from the affected EGU divided by 0.95, plus 100 percent of the useful thermal output; (e.g., steam delivered to an industrial process for a heating application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-part rule: general inclusion of 100% useful thermal output measured at SATP; special treatment for CHP facilities meeting dual ≥20% electric and thermal thresholds on a 12-month rolling average where net electric/mechanical output is adjusted (divided by 0.95) before adding useful thermal output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil-fired steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: means an electric utility steam generating unit meeting the definition of 'fossil fuel-fired' that is not a coal-fired steam generating unit, that no longer retains the capability to fire coal after December 31, 2029, and that burns oil for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during any continuous 3-calendar-year period after December 31, 2029, or for more than 15.0 percent of the annual heat input during any one calendar year after December 31, 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous structure to the natural gas-fired steam generating unit definition, using percentage thresholds and the post-2029 coal capability condition to classify units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard ambient temperature and pressure (SATP) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: means 298.15 Kelvin (25 °C, 77 °F) and 100.0 kilopascals (14.504 psi, 0.987 atm) pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies numeric SATP values and states the enthalpy of water at SATP conditions is 50 Btu/lb (used for energy measurements).

rubrics_metrics.name: State agent
rubrics_metrics.description: means an entity acting on behalf of the State, with the legal authority of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short definitional criterion for entities acting with state authority in regulatory contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stationary combustion turbine
rubrics_metrics.description: means all equipment including, but not limited to, the turbine engine, the fuel, air, lubrication and exhaust gas systems, control systems (except emissions control equipment), heat recovery system, fuel compressor, heater, and/or pump, post-combustion emission control technology, and any ancillary components and sub-components comprising any simple cycle stationary combustion turbine, any combined cycle combustion turbine, and any combined heat and power combustion turbine based system plus any integrated equipment that provides electricity or useful thermal output to the combustion turbine engine, heat recovery system, or auxiliary equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'stationary' as not self-propelled or intended to be propelled while performing its function (may be mounted on a vehicle for portability). States that a stationary combustion turbine that burns any solid fuel directly is considered a steam generating unit. Excludes emissions control equipment from the list of included control systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: means any furnace, boiler, or other device used for combusting fuel and producing steam (nuclear steam generators are not included) plus any integrated equipment that provides electricity or useful thermal output to the affected facility or auxiliary equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorizes equipment that combusts fuel to produce steam; explicitly excludes nuclear steam generators and includes integrated equipment providing electricity or useful thermal output.

rubrics_metrics.name: System Emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: means periods when the Reliability Coordinator has declared an Energy Emergency Alert level 2 or 3 as defined by NERC Reliability Standard EOP-011-2, or its successor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links definition to NERC Reliability Standard EOP-011-2 (or successor) and specific Energy Emergency Alert levels 2 and 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uprate
rubrics_metrics.description: means an increase in available electric generating unit power capacity due to a system or equipment modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers any increase in available generating capacity resulting from system/equipment changes; used to establish post-modification capacity for regulatory treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Useful thermal output
rubrics_metrics.description: means the thermal energy made available for use in any heating application (e.g., steam delivered to an industrial process for a heating application, including thermal cooling applications) that is not used for electric generation, mechanical output at the affected EGU, to directly enhance the performance of the affected EGU (e.g., economizer output is not useful thermal output, but thermal energy used to reduce fuel moisture is considered useful thermal output), or to supply energy to a pollution control device at the affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement rules: useful thermal output for affected EGU(s) with no condensate return (or where measuring condensate would not meaningfully impact emission rate calculation) is measured against energy in the thermal output at SATP. If there is meaningful energy in the condensate return (or other thermal energy input), the energy in condensate must be measured and subtracted (relative to SATP) from measured thermal output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid data
rubrics_metrics.description: means quality-assured data generated by continuous monitoring systems that are installed, operated, and maintained according to 40 CFR part 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CEMS: initial certification requirements in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendix A to 40 CFR part 75 must be met before quality-assured data are reported; ongoing QA: daily, quarterly, and semiannual/annual test requirements in sections 2.1, 2.2, and 2.3 of appendix B to 40 CFR part 75 must be met and the data validation criteria in sections 2.1.4, 2.2.3, and 2.3.2 of appendix B apply. For fuel flow meters: initial certification requirements in section 2.1.5 of appendix D to 40 CFR part 75 must be met before reporting quality-assured data (except qualifying commercial billing meters under section 2.1.4.2 of appendix D), and ongoing QA provisions in section 2.1.6 of appendix D apply (except for qualifying commercial billing meters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste-to-Energy
rubrics_metrics.description: means a process or unit (e.g., solid waste incineration unit) that recovers energy from the conversion or combustion of waste stream materials, such as municipal solid waste, to generate electricity and/or heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides illustrative example (solid waste incineration unit) and describes purpose (recover energy from waste to generate electricity and/or heat).
